pass_a_gloss: Lord, he says, your eyes are toward faith, as the eyes of the Lord are upon the righteous, for from the unrighteous he turns them away; so the eyes of the Lord toward faith, for from unbelief he turns them away. Therefore it has been well said by the one understanding what he says in the prayer: Lord, your eyes toward faith. What is written here is: Lord, your eyes toward faith. And since if a man of understanding hears a wise word he will praise it and add upon it, see how many things there are to do from Lord, your eyes toward faith. Paul says: now these three remain, faith, hope, love; and greater of these is love. As eyes of the Lord toward faith, eyes of the Lord toward hope, eyes of the Lord toward love. And since there is a spirit of power and of love and of self-control, eyes of the Lord toward love, so eyes of the Lord toward power, so eyes of the Lord toward self-control. Eyes of the Lord upon righteousness. So upon all virtues eyes of the Lord. If then you too want the rays of the intelligible eyes of God to reach upon you, take up the virtues. And it will be as Lord, your eyes toward faith, so Lord, your eyes toward each of the goods you may acquire. And if you are of such a size that the eyes of the Lord shine on you, you will say: the light of your face has been marked upon us, Lord.
pass_b_english: "Lord," he says, "your eyes are on faith" ([[Jeremiah 5:3 >> Bible:Jeremiah 5:3]]). Just as "the eyes of the Lord are on the righteous" ([[Psalm 34:15 >> Bible:Psalm 34:15]]), for he turns them away from the unrighteous, so the eyes of the Lord are on faith, for he turns them away from unbelief. So someone who understands what he is saying in prayer rightly says, "Lord, your eyes are on faith." That is what is written here: "Lord, your eyes are on faith." But since "if someone with understanding hears a wise saying, he will praise it and add to it" ([[Sirach 21:15 >> Bible:Sirach 21:15]]), see how much can be drawn from "Lord, your eyes are on faith." Paul says, "These three now remain: faith, hope, and love; but the greatest of these is love" ([[1 Corinthians 13:13 >> Bible:1 Corinthians 13:13]]). As the eyes of the Lord are on faith, so the eyes of the Lord are on hope, and the eyes of the Lord are on love.

And since there is "a spirit of power and love and self-control" ([[2 Timothy 1:7 >> Bible:2 Timothy 1:7]]), the eyes of the Lord are on love, and likewise the eyes of the Lord are on power and on self-control. [A clause appears to be missing.] The eyes of the Lord are on righteousness. In this way, the eyes of the Lord are on every virtue. So if you too want the rays of God's spiritual eyes to reach you, take up the virtues. Then, just as we say, "Lord, your eyes are on faith," we can say, "Lord, your eyes are on" each good thing you acquire. And if you have grown so far that the Lord's eyes shine upon you, you will say, "The light of your face has been marked upon us, Lord" ([[Psalm 4:6 >> Bible:Psalm 4:6]]).

variants.decision: Translate print as love; TEI is a transcription error, not a manuscript variant.

source_check_notes: Checked against Klostermann (1901), printed pp. 47–48 (PDF pp. 103–104), on 2026-09-13. The print reads ἀγάπης, “love”; the TEI transcription has ἀπάπης. At p. 48 line 6 the editor marks a possible missing clause; it is shown in brackets, without supplying his proposed reconstruction. “Spiritual eyes” translates νοητῶν ὀφθαλμῶν, eyes understood by the mind rather than bodily eyes. Psalm links use common English numbering: Psalm 34:15 = LXX 33:16; Psalm 4:6 = LXX 4:7. The wording of the latter follows the Greek quotation. This passage check does not certify the rest of the work.
